lines.speaker: Rosa Vidal
lines.text: Morning, Ivana. Rain's coming down hard again, isn't it? The market square's nearly empty.

lines.speaker: Ivana Horvat
lines.text: Rosa. Yes, the rain keeps people inside. I was just checking if any stalls bother setting up in this weather.

lines.speaker: Rosa Vidal
lines.text: I didn't see any. Just the cart tracks in the mud. Did you hear whether the council will do anything about the flooding near the lane?

lines.speaker: Ivana Horvat
lines.text: Not a word yet. They might bring it up at council day, but with this rain, who knows. You'd think they'd at least check the drains.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Rain's got the harbor quiet tonight. You here for the ledger work, or just sheltering from the weather?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Sheltering, mostly. Though I heard the chandlery's clerk position might open up soon. You know anything about that?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: I keep to the bakery mostly, so I don't follow that place. But if you're asking, maybe you've got your eye on it.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Just curious. A steady job beats waiting on the morning boat, that's all.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: True enough. Soup's decent tonight, if you're staying.

desires.title: Find work baking with flour from the island's own mill
desires.why: I came here to bake with local grain, and I got the cook job at the bakery, but I still need to see if the mill flour is used and if I can make the bread the way my father taught me.

output.summary: I arrived on the boat this morning with my suitcase and 40 coins, and I had three nights paid at the harbor inn. I went straight to the market and then to Ilić's bakery, where they took me on as cook for 3 coins a shift. I bought bread for 1 coin and ate it later. I stopped by the council hall and talked with Ivana Horvat about a leak in the roof; she said they promised to fix it before council day but that was just talk. I also saw Rosa Vidal, who told me she was elected mayor and asked what the inn needs. In the evening I went back to the inn, bought more bread, and tried to talk to someone but they were asleep. I have 2 nights left at the inn and 38 coins. I did not get to ask at the inn for help, but I did not need it since I got the bakery job.
insights: The council hall has a leak that people talk about fixing but nothing's been done yet.
Rosa Vidal is mayor now, and she seems to care about the inn's place in town.

opinions.opinion: She seems friendly, but I don't know her yet. She says she wants the inn to stay the heart of town.
She was honest about the roof leak being just talk. Seems straightforward.

intentions: I will go to the bakery for my cook shift and find out what flour they use.
I will ask about the mill and maybe visit it to see if the grain is local.
I will keep an eye on the council hall's roof leak and see if anything gets done.

self.summary: I found work as a cook at the bakery, but I still want to bake with flour from the island's mill.
self.want: To work baking with flour from the island's own mill, and to do it properly.
self.fear: That the baking traditions my father taught me might fade, especially if they use mainland flour here.
self.strangers: Gruff, but I think I was fair enough with the folks I met today.
self.advice: I argue at first, but I do follow it in the end.

projects.title: Find work baking with flour from the island's own mill
projects.progress: Got the cook job at the bakery, but haven't confirmed the flour source yet.

beliefs.belief: The bread here might be made from mainland flour, not the island's own mill.
Talk of fixing the leak is just talk until someone actually does it.

output.summary: Day one. I got off the boat with a suitcase, forty coins, and three nights prepaid at the inn. I went to the market square, then to the bakery, and I was hired on as cook there, three coins a shift. I bought bread twice during the day and ate it. I talked to Ivana Horvat at the council hall about a leak in the roof, and to Rosa Vidal at the inn. Rosa said she's mayor now. I didn't do everything I planned. I never asked at the inn for work because I got hired at the bakery first.

output.summary: Arrived this morning with 40 coins and a suitcase. Walked around, talked with Rosa Vidal and Petar Ilić, got taken on as cook at the bakery for 3 coins a shift. Bought and ate two loaves of bread. Slept at the harbor inn, two nights left paid. The rain kept much of the town quiet, but I heard the roof leak at the council hall is still unpatched and the flooding near the lane hasn't been addressed. I did not work as a field hand as planned, but I did the bakery job.
insights: Petar Ilić seems to notice details, like the damp patch, but no one has fixed it yet.
Rosa Vidal is mayor, or so I was told. She seems approachable but also cautious about the council's inaction.
The town's infrastructure has issues, like the council hall roof leak and lane flooding, that could be political points.

output.summary: Stepped off the boat this morning with 40 coins and three nights paid at the harbor inn. Took the cook shift at Ilić's bakery starting at six, and I'll be back tomorrow morning. Bought bread twice for a coin each and ate both. Spoke briefly with Rosa Vidal at the market square about the rain and whether the council would address flooding near the lane; she said nothing on it. Later, Petar Ilić and I talked at the council hall about a leak by the east window and a damp patch on the floor, and I mentioned having heard they promised to fix it before council day, but that's talk. I didn't manage the field hand work or rest I planned; the bakery work and the rain took up the day. I have 38 coins left and two more nights paid at the inn.

output.summary: Started the day getting hired as help at the inn, which felt right since that is where I belong. Earned 2 coins for a shift there. Bought bread twice to keep myself fed. I meant to talk to Petar and Ivana properly but only managed a few words with Petar at the market. Ivana said the rain is making everything damp and smelly, and we both agreed the inn floor is getting slick. The letter told me to find honest work and not borrow, and I did that. I still want to bring people together at the inn, but tonight I am just tired and glad to have a bed.
insights: The inn floor being slick is a small thing that could become a bigger problem if nobody fixes it before the rains keep coming.
Petar only said hello, so I do not know if he is open to talking more, but at least I said something.
Working at the inn again feels like coming home, even if the money is small.

opinions.opinion: He said hello but nothing more; I hope he is not avoiding me, but I will not push too hard.
She is still easy to talk to, even about the damp and the smell; I trust her enough to share small worries.

intentions: Work another shift at the inn tomorrow if they will have me.
Find time to really talk with Ivana about the inn and what it needs.
Check if anyone is doing anything about the slick floor before council day.

projects.title: Make the inn the center of the town again
projects.why: I want people to gather there like they used to.
projects.progress: Just started helping at the inn again; talked with Ivana about the damp floor but nothing more yet.

beliefs.belief: The floor is slick near the door from the rain and might need fixing before it gets worse.
She notices small problems around town and is willing to talk about them.

output.summary: Worked the morning shift at Ilić's bakery for 3 coins, bought bread twice to eat. Walked through the market and visited the council hall, but the notice board didn't tell me much. Spoke with Rosa Vidal at the inn about the rain and the state of things; she mentioned the inn's floor being slick, but I didn't check it myself. Later overheard her talking with Petar Ilić at the market. I earned 3 coins net and still have 39, with one more paid night at the inn. I didn't get much closer to knowing how the council actually works.
insights: Rosa talks about problems but doesn't seem to push for fixes before council day.
The chandlery's shutters might be warped, but I only said that to make conversation; I haven't seen them.
Bread is cheap and filling; I can keep my costs low while I settle in.

opinions.opinion: Friendly enough, but she notices problems without acting on them. Could be a rival or an ally, not sure yet.
He gave me work, that counts for something. Seems steady.

intentions: Ask Ilić if he needs me again tomorrow and keep working if the weather holds.
Spend time at the market and inn to hear who's talking about the council election.
Look at the notice board again and ask someone at the council hall how decisions get made.

The boat comes each morning; the six o'clock cart moves grain to the mill, flour to the bakery, bread and fish and apples to the market. Sundays have no shifts, Saturday is market day, the first of the month is council day.

output.summary: I woke, bought bread, worked a shift at the bakery and was paid 3 coins, bought more bread, and talked with Rosa Vidal at the inn about the damp and the boat. I also went by the council hall but I do not know what was posted. I did not do the full walk through the market or return to the inn to rest as planned; the day got away from me. I have 39 coins and one paid night left at the inn.
insights: Rosa Vidal pays attention to small problems like a slick floor; she might be worth talking to about town repairs.
The smithy is backed up on boat repairs, so nails and timber might be slow to get.

opinions.opinion: She notices practical things and is easy to talk to, but I have not seen her do anything about them.
He gave me work at the bakery; that is a start, but I still need to see how he treats people over time.

intentions: Ask at the council hall for the rules about standing for mayor and what the job actually requires.
